blocks: Figure 11 is another theoretical curvature map generated by Mendoza. The criteria for this map are dictated by K₁-K₂ relationships and do not involve mean curvature. Nonetheless, these criteria serve similar purposes and may be used as an alternative means of visualizing the surface curvature distributions.
Fig. 11 Theoretical map of local interfacial shapes for the K₁-K₂ contour plots²

Probability density plots of the mean and Gaussian curvature created from the data arrays of the three-dimensional reconstruction can be used, along with Mendoza's criteria, to identify the most probable interfacial shapes present within the microstructure. These plots for the two coarsened times are included below (Fig. 12, Fig. 13). It is clear from Figure 12 that the microstructural curvatures of the 10 minute coarsening comprise a high density of interfaces concave toward the solid, which is observed by the complex and interconnected dendritic microstructure of Figure 5. It is interesting to note that the distribution of curvature shapes encompass a wide range of curvatures (both high and low principle radii), indicating that the interfaces are homogenously short in their length scale but diverse in their curvature orientations.
Fig. 12 (left) H vs. K and (right) K₁ vs. K₂ probability density plot for the 10 minute sample

The significance of these plots, however, lies in the curvature comparison over additional coarsening durations. The plots generated for the 5 day coarsened sample (Fig. 13) show a marked change in distribution range. However, such figures must be scaled by
surface area per volume in order to account for the drastic changes in length scale between the two microstructures. The scaled K₁ vs. K₂ plots for the two samples are shown in Figure 14.
Fig. 13 (left) H vs. K and (right) K₁ vs. K₂ probability density plot for the 5 day sample

A comparison between the scaled curvature probability distribution plots illustrates curvature evolution with respect to the coarsening time. Most evident is the shift in peak density around the solid cylinder axis from 10 minutes to 5 days of coarsening. Furthermore, an increase in coarsening time appears to promote a more uniform concentration of curvatures around the peak density, as seen by the more regular spread of distributions in the 5 day sample. This uniformity around the solid cylinder peak results in an almost equal distribution on either side of the K₁ axis. An overlay of the two scaled distributions reveals that the density peak of the 5 day sample has also shifted slightly to a region of higher K curvature (smaller principle radii). Such a transition depicts a unique path of dendritic morphology toward more cylindrically shaped interfaces, which can be visually verified by the more simplistic, tubular structures present in Figure 6.
Fig. 13 SV-scaled K₁ vs. K₂ curvature distribution plots for a (top) 10 minute and (bottom) 5 day coarsened sample
